disclosures.name: TestMulUnbalanced
disclosures.reason: A MemStats bytes meter, not an AllocsPerRun one: allocBytes reads runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc around one nat.mul of a 50,000-word by a 40-word operand and asserts the bytes stay under 10 times the inputs' size. It passes on both sides at go1.24.13; at go1.26.10 Go hands nat.mul a preallocated getStack() stack, which is how Go stays near 1x (its one ~400 KB result). A thread-precise probe of the converted call shows the stack reused correctly (save, nat and restore cost 0 bytes) and an excess of about 4.2 KB in each of the ~1,249 40x40 products. 74% of it is one converted construct: an element address-of whose only use is an identity compare. alias()'s `&x[cap-1] == &y[cap-1]` mints two 184-byte element boxes per call and nat.mul calls it twice, across four mul frames per product (2,944 B); addVW's `&z[0] != &x[0]` adds 144 B. Another 21% is karatsuba's nine non-escaping `&Int{...}` locals at 96 B each (864 B). The rest is karatsuba's defer (~216 B) and basicMul (56 B). Go allocates none of these.

disclosures.name: TestNewIntAllocs
disclosures.reason: A want-zero AllocsPerRun assert over `x.Add(x, NewInt(n))`: NewInt is arranged to inline so that its `&Int{...}` and its one-word abs slice live on Go's stack. The divergence is an ORACLE-side change, not a C# regression. The test body, NewInt and Int.Add are byte-for-byte the same at go1.24.13 and go1.26.10, and the go1.24.13 page reads `fail` on both sides: Go failed this test too, so it matched. At go1.26.10 Go passes it, and C# still allocates, so it now reads Go=pass / C#=fail.

disclosures.name: TestSqrAlloc
disclosures.reason: AllocsPerRun assert new at go1.26.10 (escape_test.go:43-50): squaring an 80-word nat through Mul(x, x) must allocate at most once (the result). go1.26.10's multiplication takes its scratch from a stack (natmul.go, getStack), which Go keeps off the heap; the converted side heap-allocates that scratch and reads 4.00 objects per run on both OSes. Same Go-side change as the TestMulUnbalanced entry beside it.
